name: DeBERTa-v3 base/large + English NLI-intermediate checkpoints (MoritzLaurer *-mnli-fever-anli(-ling-wanli), tasksource, cross-encoder)

links.paper: DeBERTaV3: Improving DeBERTa using ELECTRA-Style Pre-Training with Gradient-Disentangled Embedding Sharing (He, Gao, Chen; arXiv:2111.09543, ICLR 2023); tasksource (Sileo, arXiv:2301.05948); pilot: Apaolaza Larraya et al., 'Assessing Logical Coherence of LLMs via Fine-Grained NLI', LREC 2026, pp. 5431-5444 (https://aclanthology.org/2026.lrec-1.423/)

year: 2021 (DeBERTa-v3 backbones, Nov 2021); NLI checkpoints 2022-2024 (MoritzLaurer 2022; tasksource 2023; deberta-base-long-nli 2024)
license_access: Open-weight. microsoft/deberta-v3-* MIT; MoritzLaurer NLI checkpoints MIT; tasksource/sileod checkpoints Apache-2.0. Note: downstream NLI datasets carry their own licenses (MNLI mixed/OANC, ANLI CC-BY-NC 4.0, WANLI CC-BY 4.0); the ANLI non-commercial clause is irrelevant for a shared-task submission.
track_coverage: T1 (EN) only as a first-class model. Not usable for T2 (ES), T3 (EU), or T4 (mixed) except via translate-test into English (translate ES/EU phrases to EN with NLLB/Itzuli, then classify), which inherits MT error on very short phrases.
basque_quality: None. DeBERTa-v3 was pretrained on English-only data (Wikipedia, BooksCorpus, OpenWebText, CC-News, Stories; ~160 GB) with an English 128k SentencePiece vocabulary; Basque text would be tokenized into many fragments with no semantic grounding. No Basque benchmark numbers exist; use mDeBERTa-v3 / XLM-R / Basque encoders for T3.
cross_lingual_robustness: Not applicable natively (English-only). Under translate-test the gap would be dominated by MT quality on 1-6 token phrases (headline fragments, prepositional chunks), which is where the pilot already sees most errors; expect a notably larger drop for EU than for ES. [uncertain]
architecture: Encoder-only transformer with disentangled attention (separate content and relative-position projections), trained with ELECTRA-style Replaced Token Detection and Gradient-Disentangled Embedding Sharing (GDES). Pair input '[CLS] phrase1 [SEP] phrase2 [SEP]' with a pooled-[CLS] classification head (ContextPooler + linear). NLI-intermediate checkpoints add a 3-way head (entailment / neutral / contradiction) trained on MNLI, FEVER-NLI, ANLI (+ LingNLI, WANLI for the large ling-wanli model; ~885k pairs), or on 600+ tasksource tasks for sileod/tasksource variants. For DiCo, the 3-way head is replaced by a fresh 4-way head (ignore_mismatched_sizes=True) or reused bidirectionally (see negative_other_handling).
params: deberta-v3-base: 184M total (86M backbone + 98M embedding; 12 layers, hidden 768). deberta-v3-large: 435M total (304M backbone + 131M embedding; 24 layers, hidden 1024). Vocabulary 128k.
compute: Phrase pairs are short (max_length 64 is ample). base: fine-tunes in a few minutes per run on any 16-24 GB GPU (~3k train rows, 10 epochs). large: fits comfortably on a single 24 GB GPU at batch 16-32 with max_len 64 in bf16/fp32; ~10-20 min per run on an A100; a 5-fold x 3-seed ensemble is a few GPU-hours. The pilot ran up to 150 Optuna trials/model on one A100-80GB. Known pitfall: DeBERTa-v3 is prone to fp16 overflow/NaN loss; prefer bf16 or fp32. [uncertain]
sample_efficiency: Good by encoder standards, and the main reason to use NLI-intermediate checkpoints: intermediate-task training on MNLI-style data (STILTs effect) typically stabilizes fine-tuning on ~1-3k examples and lowers seed variance, and the entailment head already encodes the directional signal needed for FE vs BE. With ~1.3k reversible source pairs (2.6k directed rows after reversal) plus ~0.5k NEGATIVE_OTHER singletons, vanilla deberta-v3-large is known to be seed-sensitive (occasional collapse runs); the pilot reported clear overfitting and unstable behavior across seeds even with dropout tuning and 150-trial searches, and large did not beat base on unseen coherence. Expect seed spread of several F1 points; mitigate with NLI-initialized weights, lr 5e-6 to 2e-5 (large) / 2e-5 to 5e-5 (base), warmup, and seed/fold ensembling. [uncertain]
reported_results: Backbones (paper/model cards): deberta-v3-large MNLI-m/mm 91.8/91.9, SQuAD2 91.5/89.0 F1/EM; deberta-v3-base MNLI-m/mm 90.6/90.7; GLUE avg (ModernBERT paper) base 88.1, large 91.4. NLI checkpoints: MoritzLaurer/DeBERTa-v3-large-mnli-fever-anli-ling-wanli accuracy MNLI-m 0.912, MNLI-mm 0.908, ANLI-all 0.702, ANLI-R3 0.64, LingNLI 0.87, WANLI 0.77 (trained on 885,242 pairs, no SNLI); MoritzLaurer/DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli MNLI-m/mm 0.903/0.903, FEVER-NLI 0.777, ANLI-all 0.579, ANLI-R3 0.495 (763,913 pairs); sileod/deberta-v3-large-tasksource-nli: 600 tasks, 80k steps, WNLI 77% zero-shot, MNLI 90% with linear probing on the frozen CLS; tasksource/deberta-base-long-nli zero-shot ANLI-A1 63.3, FEVER-NLI 79.4, FOLIO 61.8, DocNLI 90.0. Pilot on PhrasIS (weighted F1, Positives track I/H/A): DeBERTa-v3-base 0.73/0.73/0.75, large 0.71/0.72/0.76; All track base 0.87/0.88/0.88, large 0.88/0.87/0.89 (best encoder family; RoBERTa-large 0.70/0.66/0.71 Positives, ModernBERT-large 0.71/0.67/0.72). Coherence, unseen SoftCoh Positives I/H/A: base 0.84/0.78/0.84, large 0.85/0.79/0.81; unseen HardCoh Positives I/H/A: base 0.79/0.73/0.79, large 0.78/0.74/0.77; seen SoftCoh Positives-A base 0.97, large 0.94. No published phrase-level result for the NLI-intermediate checkpoints on PhrasIS/DiCo.
pilot_dico_results: Evaluated (as vanilla hub checkpoints, fine-tuned from scratch on PhrasIS with AutoModelForSequenceClassification; the NLI-intermediate MoritzLaurer/tasksource checkpoints were NOT tested). The official DiCo baseline '0.75 / 0.84 / 0.79' is DeBERTa-v3-base on the Positives combined (A) track: weighted F1 0.75 (Table 3), unseen SoftCoh 0.84 (Table 6), unseen HardCoh 0.79 (Table 7). DeBERTa-v3-large: 0.76 / 0.81 / 0.77. Caveat: the pilot label space is PhrasIS Positives (EQUI/FORW/BACK/SIMI/REL/OPPO), not the 4-way DiCo space, so numbers are indicative rather than directly comparable. Main errors: Entailment vs SIMI confusion, over-predicting SIMI under lexical overlap on Headlines, prepositional phrases, and named-entity specificity (e.g. 'Pope Francis' vs 'pope' marked equivalent).
consistency_guarantee: none (plain cross-encoder). Becomes inference-time consistent if combined with symmetric scoring/joint decoding (q(a,b) = mean of p(a,b) and Rev(p(b,a)), q(b,a) = Rev(q(a,b))).
negative_other_handling: Trained as a 4th softmax class covering all non-reversible PhrasIS relations (UNR, SIMI, REL, OPPO). In train/dev NEGATIVE_OTHER items are singletons, but nothing in the model prevents emitting NEG on one direction of a reversible pair (and FE/EQ on the other), which breaks SoftCons and costs F1. NLI heads give a useful zero-shot prior: with ent(a->b) and ent(b->a) from a bidirectional 3-way NLI pass, EQ ~ both entail, FE ~ a->b only, BE ~ b->a only, NEG ~ neither (or contradiction); PhrasIS FORW examples ('US drone strike' -> 'Drone strike', 'Mall attackers' -> 'attackers') follow premise=phrase1 entails hypothesis=phrase2, so FE aligns with standard NLI entailment [uncertain for noisy items]. SIMI/REL pairs are the hard NEG cases (pilot's dominant confusion) because NLI models trained on sentences may score high-overlap phrases as entailment.
metric_tradeoff: As a single cross-encoder it maximizes Weighted F1 (strongest encoder in the pilot) but SoftCons is only ~0.8-0.85 unseen, so HardCons trails. Adding reversal augmentation (train on both directions with Rev labels) and symmetric test-time scoring should push SoftCons toward 1.0 on pairs predicted reversible at little or no F1 cost, and HardCons rises accordingly; the remaining HardCons loss is then pure accuracy. NLI-intermediate initialization is expected to help F1 and HardCons mainly on FE/BE direction and EQ vs FE, less on NEG vs related (SIMI/REL). [uncertain]
integration: Drop-in via AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(ckpt, num_labels=4, id2label/label2id from src/labels.py, ignore_mismatched_sizes=True) + AutoTokenizer (requires sentencepiece; token_type_ids used). Encode tokenizer(p1, p2, max_length=64, truncation=True). Optionally keep the NLI head: run both directions through the 3-way head and use the 6 logits as features or as an auxiliary loss. Symmetric scoring uses REVERSE_PERM from src/labels.py: p_sym = 0.5*(p(a,b) + p(b,a)[..., REVERSE_PERM]). The repo's MLP template (src/modules/model.py) must be replaced with an HF wrapper that keeps the forward(x)->(logits, feature) contract.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes: softmax per-class probabilities; moderately over-confident after fine-tuning, so apply temperature scaling on dev (grouped by pair_id) before joint decoding / cross-view pooling.
inference_cost: Negligible: ~4k test rows x 2 directions (x views) of <=64 tokens takes seconds (base) to under a minute (large) on one GPU; a 15-model fold/seed ensemble of large is a few minutes.
rules_disclosure: Disclose: open-weight; encoder-only (DeBERTa-v3); fine-tuned; external training data = the intermediate NLI corpora baked into the checkpoint (MNLI, FEVER-NLI, ANLI, LingNLI, WANLI for MoritzLaurer large; 600+ tasksource tasks for sileod/tasksource models; SNLI+MNLI for cross-encoder); ensembling if used; translate-test MT system if used for T2-T4. No rule restricts model choice (task README: open-weight, API, fine-tuned, prompted and hybrid all allowed). tasksource's very broad training mixture makes disclosure and contamination auditing harder than for MoritzLaurer checkpoints.
contamination: Pretraining (Wikipedia, Books, OpenWebText, CC-News, Stories) may contain the underlying news headlines (iSTS/STS headlines were drawn from news feeds) but not the phrase-level labels; low risk. MNLI/FEVER/ANLI/LingNLI/WANLI do not contain PhrasIS/iSTS phrase pairs; SNLI (in cross-encoder checkpoints) shares the Flickr caption domain with the PhrasIS Images subset but not the pairs. A grep of the current tasksource task registry found no PhrasIS or iSTS task; older tasksource checkpoint mixtures were not audited [uncertain]. The real risk is PhrasIS itself: its labeled train and test splits are public (e.g. in the pilot repo), DiCo test pairs are derived from PhrasIS, and the organizers' PhrasIS data-use policy is still pending; any use of PhrasIS beyond the official DiCo train must be grouped by source pair and disclosed.
structural_cue_dependence: None intrinsically: the model sees only the two phrases. Any pair_id/singleton heuristic would be an external post-processing choice.
expected_gain: Primary Track 1 backbone and the reference to beat. Expected: MoritzLaurer/DeBERTa-v3-large-mnli-fever-anli-ling-wanli fine-tuned on DiCo with reversal augmentation should match or exceed the pilot's 0.75 F1 while reducing seed variance; together with symmetric scoring/joint decoding, SoftCons near 1.0 on predicted-reversible pairs and HardCons roughly equal to pairwise accuracy (plausibly 0.80+ on T1). Rationale: best family in the pilot; NLI-intermediate training directly encodes directional entailment; cheap enough for 5-fold x multi-seed ensembles. Compare base vs large and MoritzLaurer vs tasksource on grouped CV, since the pilot saw no consistent large > base advantage on unseen coherence. [uncertain]
